event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. event.summary: An old page can interpret pasted JSON as terminal commands
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: a page left open through the grid-only update can send a pasted JSON document as a terminal-input instruction. Instead of inserting the document, it inserts the document's data field; escaped carriage returns become real Enter input outside bracketed paste, allowing commands embedded in otherwise literal pasted JSON to run. This preserves and strengthens l1's original suspected unintended-input consequence; c3's ordinary-key attachment failure still applies to non-JSON input. Source route: at the parent revision, a refreshed listing missing agent_terminal defaults to None (lib.rs:514-521), agent_spec_kind preserves it (session_view.rs:3839-3849), and terminal.js:4651-4666 constructs xterm for unknown kind. Missing stream notices choose bytes (:5721-5723, :5891-5930). The shipped paste handler inserts text (:2650-2675), insert sanitizes only literal ESC markers (:2232-2235 and term-bytes.js:55-56), and the installed callback invokes term.paste (:4628-4634). The removed xterm bundle's paste implementation calls triggerDataEvent once with the whole prepared text and brackets it only when its own decPrivateModes.bracketedPasteMode is true; that mode defaults false (source at the parent xterm.js:1). Thus a fresh legacy surface can send a complete small one-line JSON text payload unchanged. Its onData callback and sendData encode that text into one WebSocket binary message (parent terminal.js:4157-4158, :4191-4196). The reviewed helm relays each message as one frame per SPEC_impl.md, 'Grid streams'. GridInput uses serde(tag = 't') and its Text variant holds data (grid.rs:1565-1566, :1610-1612); decode deserializes JSON and validates its length, not its client provenance (:1650-1655, :1686-1693). HostAttach::send_input decodes it before encoding (:1064-1076); InputEncoder encodes Text as data.as_bytes() without paste wrapping (grid_input.rs:175). JSON string escapes therefore become actual terminal control bytes although the user's original pasted document contained only literal backslashes and letters. The supervisor's real bracketed-paste mode does not protect a Text message. Suggested bucket: highest/security or loss of work, because an established shipped paste route can turn literal document text into unbracketed command input. Confidence: likely, with the stated premise that the old page has mounted a fresh xterm surface after a listing without kind and remains attached until the paste; source establishes that surface's default unbracketed mode and complete-message paste dispatch. No runtime behavior was observed. proposed_drop: potential specification acceptance requires independent judgment, not accepted here. Exact text in SPEC_impl.md:3022-3029, 'Grid streams': 'A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working.' and 'Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy.' That paragraph explicitly describes misdrawing and malformed-input detachment, but does not specifically name successful reinterpretation of a valid pasted JSON document as unbracketed program input. The original full paragraph is preserved in c3. possible_cover: none; forbidden coverage sources were not consulted. Caveats: this needs an old page, an unknown-kind mount and pasted text shaped as a valid small GridInput Text message; ordinary keystrokes generally end the attachment instead. Program-provided output that happened to enable the old xterm surface's paste mode could prevent this particular route. No reproduction, test or build performed. Fix direction: preserve old-page grid negotiation or reject incompatible browser input before relaying it, so old raw text cannot be accepted as grid control.
